title: Liquid reservoir: fractional capacity & tenancy circuit (PRD sketch)
body:
Purpose & high-level idea:

This doc sketches a 'liquid reservoir' model for Dedicated capacity that treats fractional, short-lived capacity as a fluid pool that can be borrowed by tenants under controlled QoS and billing rules. The goal is to offer predictable steady-state reservations while allowing cost-effective, elastic burst for short spikes without heavy pre-provisioning or hard preemption.

Problem we are solving:
- Customers with predictable baseline and occasional micro/macro bursts want lower committed costs but occasional higher throughput.
- Current reserved-only model forces over-commit or complex manual burst requests.
- Hard preemption and evictions are painful for latency-sensitive requests and for customer trust.
- We need an autoscaling/burst fabric with clear semantics, observable economics, and strong isolation boundary guarantees.

Goals & success metrics:
- Offer fractional-burst capacity that reduces committed GPU hours by ~15–40% for typical customers with bursty workloads.
- Maintain 99.9% latency SLO for steady-state lanes; best-effort for burst lanes but with well-defined fallback.
- Reduce emergency manual interventions for Dedicated customers by 50% vs baseline.
- Provide per-tenant visibility for borrowed capacity and clear billing attribution.

Non-goals:
- Not a replacement for Dedicated full-reserve for sustained high-throughput tenants.
- Not intended to support unlimited burst across all tenants (we cap and gate).

Core concepts:
1) Reservoir pool: a cluster-level pool of ephemeral compute capacity (fractional slices of GPU-backed slots) that can be drawn by tenants that opt-in. The pool is time-windowed and replenishes like a reservoir.
2) Tenancy circuit: each tenant has a "circuit" with three channels — steady (reserved), buffer (pre-warmed soft slots), and surge (liquid reservoir draws). Each channel has different isolation and billing semantics.
3) Credit rate & decay: tenants receive a 'headroom' credit budget based on commit tier and historical usage. Credits accrue/decay on a sliding window (e.g., per-hour rolling).
4) Soft preemption & graceful degrade: reservoir evictions prioritize requests by SLO weight, and attempts graceful fallback to lower-fidelity model variants or degraded lanes instead of hard kill.

Proposed design (high level):
- Pool allocation: A percentage of cluster capacity is designated as the liquid reservoir. Operator-settable per-region. Initially 8–12% recommended for early experiments.
- Tenant opt-in: Customers choose a "burst profile" at purchase: none, modest, aggressive. Profile controls credit accrual rate, max concurrent reservoir draws, and price multiplier.
- Credit accounting: Daily/hourly ledger per tenant. Borrowing consumes credits; credits regenerate according to baseline commit and any purchased burst packs. We track two counters: instantaneous concurrent draws and rolling token consumption.
- Admission control: Requests routed through quota service. If steady capacity exhausted, buffer lanes (short-lived warm containers) attempted; if buffer exhausted and tenant has credits, reservoir draw attempted. Admission enforces per-tenant max-concurrency, per-model compatibility, and cost guardrails.
- Execution & isolation: Reservoir slices run in sandboxed slices (cgroups + network policy) with tighter I/O and cross-tenant throttles. KV cache eviction policies favor steady lanes; reservoir slices use read-through caches and may have slower cold-starts.
- Fallback chain: reservoir -> degraded model variant (quantized / lower-fidelity) -> hosted fallback (if customer allows) -> queue with ETA. Each step records event for observability and billing reconciliation.

APIs & config (customer-facing):
- Purchase params: burst_profile {none|modest|aggressive}, burst_pack_units (optional prepaid credits), max_burst_concurrency, allowed_model_variants (opt-in for degraded fallback).
- Runtime API (management): getCreditBalance(), requestBurst(tokens, concurrency_hint), setFallbackPolicy({use-degraded:true, allow-hosted:false}).
- Billing: explicit line item for 'liquid-reservoir usage' with units=credit-tokens and an attached price multiplier.

Operational concerns & telemetry:
- Telemetry must include: credit delta timelines, reservoir draws (start/stop), failed reservoir admissions and reason codes, fallback events, per-tenant P50/P95 latency across channels, cost-per-token breakdown.
- Alerting: when reservoir pool utilization exceeds 70% sustained 15m => ops review; when single tenant uses >X% of reservoir for >Y minutes => auto-throttle & paging.
- Cost model: per-token cost estimated from occupancy-weighted GPU minute cost + overhead. Provide projected monthly spend given historical burst shape.

Isolation & safety mechanisms:
- Circuit breakers: hard per-tenant caps (concurrency and total hourly tokens).
- Fairness allocator: proportional share with priority weights; prevents single tenant from starving others.
- Tenant sandboxing: strict network + disk quotas for reservoir slices. No shared local KV unless explicitly pinned.
- Eviction policy: least-priority reservoir tasks preempted first; graceful termination tries model checkpointing/KV snapshot for quick resume.

Rollout plan (phases):
- Phase 0 (lab): internal-only with synthetic burst workloads. Validate credit accounting, admission flows, basic telemetry.
- Phase 1 (alpha): small set (5) of trusted customers, opt-in only, reservoir=8% in a single region. Collect data on economics & SLO.
- Phase 2 (beta): expand to 50 customers, introduce pricing tiers, test cross-region reservoir pooling.
- Phase 3 (GA): full product with console UI, SLAs for steady lanes, documented pricing.

Migration & customer UX:
- Customers on existing Dedicated plans get default burst_profile=none. Offer one-click opt-in with simulated cost preview based on past 30d usage.
- Provide 'dry-run' mode that simulates draws and shows how outages/fallbacks would have behaved.

Acceptance criteria for moving from alpha -> beta:
- No more than 2 customer-impacting reservoir incidents (lost steady SLO) in 30 days.
- Credit accounting matches billing to within 1% in reconciliation window.
- Observability dashboards for per-tenant reservoir usage and fallback events.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- How to price burst credits to align incentives? Flat multiplier vs dynamic spot pricing?
- Centralized reservoir vs zone-local reservoirs (latency & fault domain tradeoffs).
- How much of cluster to commit to reservoir without impacting steady lanes? Conservative default vs adaptive tuning.
- Integration with Dedicated SLA: should customers be able to purchase reservoir-backed soft-SLA?

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: noisy tenant exhausts reservoir and impacts others. Mitigation: strict concurrency caps + fairness allocator + real-time throttles.
- Risk: billing disputes from opaque fallback chains. Mitigation: clear per-event logs, refund playbook, customer-facing timeline.
- Risk: operator complexity / debugging headache. Mitigation: start small, build rich telemetry, runbook for typical incidents.

Next steps / TODOs:
- [Engineering] spike: admission controller prototype + per-tenant ledger (2 weeks) — assignee: Riley Chen
- [Product] pricing experiment matrix and customer offer language — assignee: Asha Patel
- [SRE] define pool sizing heuristics + alerting thresholds — assignee: Marco Ruiz
- [Legal/Billing] draft T&C addendum for burst billing and dispute resolution — assignee: Priya Singh
- Schedule sync with 3 pilot customers for alpha onboarding (target start: 2025-04-01).

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- Could pair reservoir with model-aware admission (prefer to route compute-heavy but low-quality requests to quantized variants first).
- Consider offering 'burst insurance' where customers buy guarantee of no preemption for a short window at higher price.
- Add a small UX panel in console showing "how many bursts you used this month" with cost impact and tips to reduce.

References & related work:
- See linked RFC in GitHub for preliminary admission control design (linked_artifacts).
- Internal sim notebook: (not linked here) used to tune credit decay rates.

Unresolved: define exact credit accrual curve (linear vs exponential decay). Need to run sims on 30M request traces.

-- end of sketch --

Comments welcome — flagging for architecture review and economics model session next week.
short_summary: Draft PRD sketch for a "liquid reservoir" fractional burst fabric on Dedicated: credit-based borrowing, tenancy circuits, soft preemption, and billing/observability proposals.
